info.title: Bidora pilot email verification
info.description: Consumes one approved email-ownership token atomically. It creates no session, membership, capability, or tenant context.

x-approval.evidence: approved email verification token policy and subsequent proceed

post.summary: Request a replacement email verification token
post.description: Returns the same accepted response for unknown, malformed, verified, disabled and delivery-ambiguous targets. Every request consumes the approved fail-closed registration identity and network limits. A successful issuance atomically invalidates the previous active token before delivery. This operation creates no session or authority.

202.description: Generic accepted response. Delivery and account existence are not disclosed.

X-Bidora-Code-Challenge.description: Random per-request reference for the new six-digit code, including for ineligible targets.

429.description: Fail-closed attempt denial with the effective remaining quota/block wait.

post.description: Requires an exact approved HTTPS Origin and trusted network context for six-digit codes. New codes are numeric, scoped to a random reference and purpose through a server HMAC, with per-reference failure limits and network limits. Legacy strong tokens remain valid. Codes are supplied only in strict JSON, never in URLs. Invalid, expired, consumed and unknown tokens return the same failure. Success does not authenticate the browser or grant tenant authority.

token.description: Six numeric digits with challenge_ref, or a legacy 43-character token.

challenge_ref.description: Required with six digits; random per-request reference supplied by the issuance response and email link.

204.description: Email ownership verified. No body, cookies, or session.

400.description: Malformed request or generic invalid, expired, unknown, or consumed token.

Failure.description: Safe failure without token, identity, or dependency details.
